name: Eber
overview: Eber is a male descendant of the tribe of Benjamin, specifically identified as the son of Elpaal according to 1 Chronicles 8:12. Beyond this unique attribute, there are no additional personal notes provided in the Scripture. His lineage places him within the genealogical records of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Eber means '[regions] beyond [the river],' reflecting a geographical or ancestral designation rather than a divine title. This proper name was not given by God but is recorded in 1 Chronicles 8:12, indicating his identity within the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Eber is the son of Elpaal, as noted in 1 Chronicles 8:12. No other family relationships are detailed in the provided information, and thus no further familial connections can be asserted beyond this father-son relationship.
scriptureSignificance: Eber holds significance as a key figure in the biblical genealogy, serving as a link in the lineage from Noah to Abraham. He is recognized as the ancestor after whom the Hebrew people are named, marking him as foundational in preserving the godly line through the generations following the flood. His place in Scripture underscores the continuity of God's covenantal promises through the descendants of Shem.
